title: "Why Your Julia Loop Is Slow"
description: "Type stability, in one example"
date: 2026-10-02

---

A common surprise for new Julia users is that a loop can be fast or slow
depending on whether the compiler can infer types.

```{julia}
function sum_unstable(xs)
    total = 0          # starts as an Int
    for x in xs
        total += x     # becomes a Float64 if xs holds floats
    end
    return total
end

function sum_stable(xs)
    total = zero(eltype(xs))
    for x in xs
        total += x
    end
    return total
end

xs = rand(10^6)
sum_stable(xs) ≈ sum_unstable(xs)
```

```{julia}
#| output: false
using BenchmarkTools
```

```{julia}
@btime sum_unstable($xs)
@btime sum_stable($xs)
```

A static REPL excerpt, shown but not executed:

```julia
julia> @code_warntype sum_unstable(xs)
  total::Union{Float64, Int64}
```
